place.source_title: Speed Changing Pulley Company Factory, Thirty-second Street

brief: Early motor-industry works on the edge of the mill district: a two-storey office block of white-painted brick with a row of round-arched windows and a small porch at the door, joined to a long one-storey brick shop lit by tall segmental windows and a clerestory monitor down the ridge. Built in 1908 as the first plant lured to town by a businessmen's bonus scheme; loading doors and a gravel yard face the rail spur.

facade.notes: the Speed Changing Pulley Co. office (Anderson IN, 1908), HAER: a two-storey white-painted brick office block with round-arched upper windows and a corbelled arcaded cornice, a small hooded door, a lawn; low flat-roofed factory sheds behind -- the front office as the factory's face to the street

why.note: the works' office faces the street with a lawn; the sheds behind face the rail siding
